normative_interpretations: ADD v1.3 section 1.4: every event belongs to exactly one GovernedContext; indexes are not shared across incompatible isolation tuples. Section 3.2: idempotency_key deduplicates the logical event; ordering only per ordering key. Two events of different contexts are never the same logical event, so dedup and ordering state are scoped by context.

Chosen key: the PoC CanonicalIngestionEnvelope carries the context only as governed_context_digest, the digest of the whole GovernedContext (which includes the isolation tuple). Equal digest implies equal isolation tuple; two digests with an equal isolation tuple but different other GovernedContext fields are treated as different contexts. This errs toward publishing a possible duplicate rather than dropping or quarantining another context's event (no silent cross-context loss); full isolation-tuple construction from the envelope is outside the 14-field PoC envelope and outside this remediation.

requirement_results.command: two Governed Contexts reusing one idempotency_key both reach the real topic (exact record set read from Kafka end offsets), no quarantine; replaying each afterwards adds nothing (RED on c2f9e50: context B's event silently dropped)
same context and same idempotency_key: exactly one record on the real topic, no quarantine (positive guard of the unchanged INFO-A option-1 behaviour; passes on c2f9e50 too)

same aggregate_ref in two contexts: context B sequence 1 after context A sequence 5 is accepted; inside one context a non-advancing sequence (lower or equal) is still quarantined OUT_OF_ORDER and never reaches the topic, while each context advances only its own watermark (RED on c2f9e50: OUT_OF_ORDER from the other context's sequence)

through EventOperationsCoordinator: publish_with_backpressure of both contexts reusing a key delivers both with no dead letter; replay of a context-B dead letter is published although context A used the key; replay of an already-durable same-context event stays a no-op (RED on c2f9e50: context B's record missing)

governed_context_digest empty, None or non-string: BackboneError MISSING_CONTEXT, quarantined, nothing published, never deduplicated against shared state (RED on c2f9e50: DID NOT RAISE, dropped as a replay of the shared key)

residual_risks: Dedup and ordering state are in memory and lost on restart (LLD v1.1 section 6 'deduplica durable'): allocated to OCOR-DEV-REM-0026 (INFO-C), which must preserve this isolation scoping.
Same-key/different-payload reuse inside one context is still dropped as a replay without quarantine or audit (INFO-A option 1, note for a future normative decision).
Two GovernedContext digests that share the isolation tuple are deduplicated separately (see normative_interpretations): possible duplicate publication, never silent loss.
The quarantine list of one backbone instance is shared across contexts (an append-only record, not dedup/ordering state); exposure of quarantine to callers is not policy-filtered by this component.
CanonicalEventBackbone and EventOperationsCoordinator are not yet used by other ocor-runtime modules (INFO-A audit); G6 ingestion qualification (BA-07, FR-069..FR-075) depends on them.
